advances: Ordinary volume and actual balanced coareas for one explicit family; no general joint-row or mixed-integer assertion.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The edge matrix based at $P_0$ is $(t+C)I+(A/d-C)\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^\top$ with determinant $(t+C)^{d-1}(A+B)\ne0$. The barycentric weights $B/(A+B)$ at $P_0$ and $A/[d(A+B)]$ at each other vertex are positive, sum to one and give zero, using $\sum_{j\ge1}P_j=B\mathbf{1}$. Row zero has vertex margins $A,-B,\ldots,-B$; row $j\ge1$ has margins $-A/d,t,-C,\ldots,-C$ with $t$ at $P_j$. No vertex is on the plane. The displayed normals sum to zero and have minimal positive dependence.

A simplex cap with sole positive vertex margin $a$ and negative margins $-b_l$ has fraction $a^d/\prod_l(a+b_l)$, by the ratios of the cut edges. Its normalized coarea is $d/a$ times its volume fraction by the pyramid volume formula, using the altitude $a/\|v_i\|$. Apply this to row zero and the complements of rows $j\ge1$, which share the same sections. Their data are
$
Q_0=(A/(A+B))^d,\quad S_0=dA^{d-1}/(A+B)^d,\qquad
Q_j=1-A^d/D^{d-1},\quad S_j=d^2A^{d-1}/D^{d-1}.
$
For the complementary caps the edge denominators are one $A/d+t=1/d$ and $d-1$ copies of $A/d-C=D/d$. Therefore $M=D^{d-1}/(dA^{d-1})$, $f_0=dA^{d-1}(A+B)/D^{d-1}$, and $f_j=Q_j^{(d-1)/d}=:x\in(0,1)$ for all $j\ge1$. Substitution gives
$
\Phi_0=d-1+\frac{A^{d-1}[1-d(d-1)C]}{(A-dC)^{d-1}}.
$
For $u=-dC/A>0$ the added fraction is $[1+(d-1)Au]/(1+u)^{d-1}<1$ by Bernoulli and $A<1$. It tends to one as $C\uparrow0$.

For the two-level comparison maximize in $z$ at $d-(d-1)x^p$. Put $U=1+(d-1)(x-x^p)/d$. The derivative of $x+(d-1)U^p$ is $1-U^{1/(d-1)}[dr-(d-1)]$, where $r=x^{1/(d-1)}$. This is positive if $dr\le d-1$. Otherwise put $w=1-r\in[0,1/d)$, so $U\le1+(d-1)w/d$. Then
$
U(1-dw)^{d-1}\le(1+(d-1)w/d)(1-dw)\le1
$
with strictness for $w>0$. The function increases strictly below $x=1$, at which its value is $d$. The selected row gives the required budget for $z=f_0$, proving strictness of all other rows.

statement:
For $d\ge2$, $0<A<1$, and $C<0$ with $C\ne-t$, set $t=(1-A)/d$, $B=t-(d-1)C$, $D=A-dC$. Let $K$ be the simplex with $P_0=-(A/d)\mathbf{1}$ and $P_j=(t+C)e_j-C\mathbf{1}$ for $1\le j\le d$, and take the through-origin caps for the actual balanced normal circuit $v_0=-\mathbf{1},\ v_j=e_j$. The common mark is interior. The first cap strictly contains one vertex and each remaining cap strictly contains $d$ vertices. Let $Q_i=|K\cap\{v_i\cdot x\ge0\}|/|K|$, $S_i=\mathcal H^{d-1}(K\cap v_i^\perp)/(|K|\|v_i\|)$, $M=\sum_iQ_i/S_i$, and $f_i=dQ_i^{(d-1)/d}/(S_iM)$. For $p=d/(d-1)$ all joint rows $\Phi_i=f_i+(d-1)[(\sum_{j\ne i}f_j)/d]^p$ are strictly less than $d$, and $\Phi_0\to d$ as $C\uparrow0$.

More generally for $0\le x\le1,\ 0\le z\le d-(d-1)x^p$,
$
x+(d-1)\left(\frac{z+(d-1)x}{d}\right)^p\le d ,
$
strictly for $x<1$.
title: All joint rows stay strict in an incidence-changing simplex family
